1.why: All seven screens are static with generous whitespace and no pop-ups or animations, though the persistent dark Logs panel adds some visual weight.

2.why: Primary actions appear as bold blue buttons and the current step is highlighted in the progress pills, so key elements stand out on every screen.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task under a clear heading ('verify your recovery code', 'choose a strong password'), making the needed item easy to locate.

4.why: The four steps are always visible in the progress indicator and instructions appear on-screen when needed, so little must be memorized, though the password policy lists several character rules.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password manager prompt, or autofill option is visible on any screen; only plain input fields appear.

6.why: Previously issued codes remain visible in the Logs panel across screens aiding recognition, but there are no saved-login or familiar-item features.

7.why: Main UI text is short and plain ('Choose one clear next step'), though the Logs panel uses technical jargon like 'Mock MFA delivery'.

8.why: No error state or error message is shown in any of the seven screenshots, so this claim cannot be confirmed.

9.why: The Logs panel shows the exact code to type, but no example is given for creating the password or filling other fields.

10.why: The options shown (reset vs. sign in, verify vs. request new code) are clearly labeled, but there is no choice among login methods such as face login—only a fixed password-plus-code path.

11.why: No screen offers more than two or three actions at once; most screens present a single primary button.

12.why: Green confirmation banners and log entries state the result of every action ('You are securely signed in', 'Request confirmed', 'You have completed all steps').

13.why: Every screen includes a 'Help and safety' section, a footer help note, and short per-step tips, though the help section is collapsed by default.

14.why: A 'Request a new code' button and 'Continue using simulated link' option allow recovery from mistakes, and the footer states users can pause and return without rushing.

15.why: All seven screens share an identical layout—header, step pills, white card with heading, primary button, Help section, Logs panel, and footer—supporting learnability.
